title: Sorafenib: differentiated thyroid cancer
indication_text: Progressive, locally advanced or metastatic differentiated thyroid cancer that no longer responds to radioactive iodine.
purpose: This treatment aims to slow cancer growth and help control symptoms. Your team explains the expected benefit, uncertainty and alternatives for your situation.
schedule_summary: Sorafenib 400 mg twice daily, every day, until progression or unacceptable side effects.
administration_text: Take with water, without food or with a low- or moderate-fat meal. For a high-fat meal, take sorafenib at least 1 hour before or 2 hours afterwards. Follow the prescribed morning and evening doses; never change the dose yourself.
monitoring_summary: Consider blood count, kidney and liver tests at Day 14 of the first month. Repeat these bloods and thyroid tests every 28 days. Check blood pressure weekly in month 1, then every 28 days; check INR as indicated if taking warfarin.

agents.name: Sorafenib
agents.explanation: Sorafenib blocks several enzymes involved in signals that help cancer cells grow and new blood vessels form. It can also affect healthy blood vessels, skin and thyroid hormone control.
agents.watch: Tell the team before surgery or dental procedures. Report painful palms or soles early; skin care and early dose review can help prevent severe hand-foot reactions.
risks: Painful palms and soles (hand-foot skin reaction), rash and hair thinning
Diarrhoea, tiredness, reduced appetite and weight loss
High blood pressure and thyroid hormone changes
Bleeding, heart ischaemia and impaired wound healing
Rare bowel perforation, severe liver injury and severe skin reactions
Low blood sugar, especially with diabetes treatment; possible effects on fertility and pregnancy

anatomy: Balance activity and rest. Sudden confusion, seizure, severe headache or a change in vision needs urgent help.
Report ulcers, pain, dry mouth, difficulty swallowing or weight loss early. Ask for oral care, dietetic and swallowing support.
Follow prescribed heart and blood-pressure checks. Chest pain, fainting, palpitations or new breathlessness needs urgent advice.
New cough or breathlessness needs prompt review; serious causes include infection or lung injury.
Use prescribed support. Report persistent diarrhoea or vomiting, inability to drink, blood or severe abdominal pain.
Report reduced urine, swelling or poor fluid intake; keep blood and urine tests.
Report painful palms or soles, rash or blistering early. Severe spreading rash or mouth/eye involvement needs urgent review.
Discuss fertility preservation, contraception, pregnancy and breastfeeding before starting.

evidence.title: What the evidence can tell you
evidence.intro: Research supports a treatment discussion; it cannot predict one person’s outcome.
evidence.population: Progressive, locally advanced or metastatic differentiated thyroid cancer that no longer responds to radioactive iodine.
evidence.comparison: Placebo in the cited randomised trial
evidence.interpretation: DECISION, a randomised placebo-controlled study in radioactive-iodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer, reported median progression-free survival of 10.8 versus 5.8 months (hazard ratio 0.587; 95% CI 0.454–0.758). The cited overall-survival analysis did not show a statistically significant difference. Progression-free survival measures time without progression or death, not a predicted lifespan.
limitations: Trial populations and schedules differ; comparisons across separate trials are unreliable.
An improvement in progression-free survival is not automatically an overall-survival benefit.

consent_support: Discuss treatment aim, expected benefit and uncertainty, alternatives and the option of declining; each medicine’s risks, potentially lasting effects, required tests, urgent symptoms, fertility, contraception, pregnancy, breastfeeding and the individual support plan.
